Transport & itineraries · Ellora Cave 16

Kailasa Temple One-Hour Visit

With roughly an hour for the monument itself, stay with Cave 16. Admission, the walk from the gate and the return are separate from that hour.

Google Maps ↗ ASI source listing ↗

Independent guide · Page reviewed 9 November 2026 · ASI listing consulted 2026-10-29

Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is one monument within the UNESCO-listed Ellora Caves. Prices, opening status and routes are dated listings to re-check, not live confirmations.

  1. Kailasa Temple Verul
  2. Transport & itineraries
  3. Kailasa Temple One-Hour Visit

Before the clock starts

A one-hour visit means one hour at the monument, not one hour from arrival. Entry procedures, the walk inside the property and the return to your vehicle all sit outside it. Confirm the ASI sunrise-to-sunset window and weekly Tuesday closure first.

Use the verified map link to agree the gate and meeting point with your driver; a UNESCO property coordinate is not an entrance.

A practical sequence

Move from the whole to the detail: take in the excavated courtyard and the surrounding rock walls, then the carved upper facades, then one or two sculptural panels. UNESCO highlights the Ravana shaking Mount Kailasa scene and painting traces on the front mandapa ceiling.

Treat this as an order of attention, not a timed guarantee. Closed areas, conservation work and your own pace take priority.

What to leave out

Do not try to add Cave 10, the Indra Sabha or a regional fort to this plan. If you have more time, the half-day and one-day itinerary pages cover those combinations. ASI suggests a 3–4 hour visit for a focused selection of Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34.

Suggested order

  1. Agree the gate and meeting point
  2. Complete admission and walk to Cave 16
  3. Read the excavated courtyard and rock walls
  4. Study the upper carved facades
  5. Focus on one sculptural panel, such as the Ravana relief
  6. Return to the agreed pick-up point

An order of attention, not a timed guarantee. Closed areas, conservation work and your own pace take priority.

Frequently asked questions

Is one hour enough for Kailasa Temple?

It is enough for a focused look at Cave 16 itself, but not for the wider ensemble. Add separate time for admission and walking.

What should I prioritise?

The courtyard volume, the carved upper facades and one major sculptural panel. UNESCO highlights the Ravana relief and front mandapa ceiling painting traces.

Can I include other caves?

Not comfortably in an hour. See the half-day itinerary for a realistic combination.
